thread:
alex: Heads-up — noticed an uptick in resume/reconnect rates from our proxy pool since yesterday evening. Graphs show a hard step in observed holdoff TTLs from ~60s to ~8s.
maya: huh that's a big change. any recent rollouts to the proxy or sticky-routing config? :thinking:
alex: can confirm a small canary to proxy v2.3 went out last night (20%) for latency improvements. rollout notes said no behavioral changes to resume handling but telemetry seems to disagree.
jin: stack trace / logs? I can grep the proxy logs for resume reasons.
alex: pasted a tiny slice from client-side logs and proxy headers we see in console trace:
```
Client: SSE reconnect after 9s, resume-token=abc123
Proxy: X-Resume-Holdoff: 8
Proxy: X-Route-Policy: shard-sticky
```
We used to see X-Resume-Holdoff: 60 in previous runs.
sam: could be a default TTL change in the new proxy code — maybe the backoff config got flattened for faster recovery? that would explain more frequent reconnect churn and billing replays.
maya: frequent reconnects could double-bill some resumed sessions depending on how quota events are deduped in the billing pipeline. we should check console per-route billing spikes around that time.
ops-bot: deploy v2.3 to proxy-pool-1 completed at 2026-03-20T19:02:11Z :white_check_mark:
jin: searching logs now... found a config diff in the canary: `resume_holdoff_secs` was accidentally set to 8 in the config template because a previously deprecated default was reintroduced.
alex: ugh. so intended optimization inadvertently reduced conservative holdoff. We need a mitigation plan before scaling canary.
maya: immediate actions: (1) rollback canary from 20% -> 0% on proxy-pool-1, (2) add alert on route-level holdoff < 30s, (3) patch console to surface X-Resume-Holdoff header in trace view for last 24h. thoughts?
sam: agree. also add a short-term client-side smoothing of jitter to avoid synchronized reconnects. i can ship a client lib patch to add randomized backoff up to +50% jitter.
jin: rollback in progress, PR for alerting + dashboard card up: #4523. For telemetry we currently only index route and error; need to add header extraction for resume_holdoff. small change to trace pipeline but should be quick.
alex: UX ask for console: when holdoff < configured SLO, show a yellow badge in stream session view and a direct link to rollout that touched that route. helps on-call link to root cause quicker.
maya: agree on badge. also record the rollout id in the trace before the connector finishes — right now rollout metadata is only attached at deploy time, not to live sessions.
sam: client patch + runtime revert should buy us time. i'll coordinate a client canary and post rollout notes.
alex: after rollback we should re-run a 5% canary with explicit `resume_holdoff_secs: 60` in the deploy template and monitor for delta. Also add a backfill job to reconcile any double-billing suspected between 19:00-22:00.
ops-bot: rollback job initiated: proxy-pool-1 -> v2.2 (triggered by alex) :rocket:
jin: rollback done, observed holdoff header back at ~60s in traces. starting dashboard snippet to show holdoff distribution per-route.
alex: thanks. follow-ups: small RFC to make resume_holdoff config explicit in rollout UI (template override) and a telemetry contract doc so kernel teams know which headers we rely on. i'll open RFC after lunch.
maya: filing billing reconcile ticket now.
sam: will open client patch PR  and coordinate release notes.
alex: cool. big takeaway: perf rollouts can change defensive defaults; need guardrails.`
